title: Band-Pass Filter - GPS L1 (1575 MHz) for Millimeter-Wave Beamforming
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Ana Reyes

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Band-Pass Filter filter targeting GPS L1 (1575 MHz) for Millimeter-Wave Beamforming. The filter is designed on 36° YX LiTaO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 749.6 MHz and bandwidth of 345.7 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Millimeter-Wave Beamforming module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Band-Pass Filter
- Frequency Band: GPS L1 (1575 MHz)
- Application: Millimeter-Wave Beamforming
- Substrate: 36° YX LiTaO3
- Package: CSP (Chip Scale Package)
- Design Tool: CST Studio Suite 2024
- Design Center: Osaka Design Center

This specification applies to all variants of the Band-Pass Filter design targeting GPS L1 (1575 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       749.6 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       345.7 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.0 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 13.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 30.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 42.0 dB
Q Factor:               12780
Temperature Coefficient:-5.7 ppm/°C
Die Size:               0.6 x 2.2 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   6
Electrode Material:     W
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open CST Studio Suite 2024 and load the Band-Pass Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 36° YX LiTaO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 749.6 MHz, BW 345.7 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.0 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (CSP (Chip Scale Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, 36° YX LiTaO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNA67.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 2249 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.0 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 13.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 519 MHz offset >= 30.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 7 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 0.5 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +28 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 2000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 97%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-03-11
Devices Tested:         82
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.69 dB
Return Loss (meas):     15.3 dB
Rejection (meas):       32.6 dB
Isolation (meas):       47.3 dB
Q Factor (meas):        12780
Group Delay Variation:  4.7 ns
Power Handling:         +35 dBm
Die Yield:              93.9%

Result Classification:  CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Band-Pass Filter design demonstrated acceptable performance for GPS L1 (1575 MHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Group delay flatness improved compared to previous revision.
e) ESD robustness exceeded specification by 2x margin.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
